subject: Post-demo: Integral.ai inference playbook & policy handoff
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@integral.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:32:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Integral.ai inference playbook & policy handoff

Hi Samir — thanks again for a really productive demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Key takeaways
- Primary workload: high-throughput customer chat classification + on-demand summarization for audit trails.
- Peak QPS expected: ~120 requests/s, p95 latency target: <= 300ms for short responses (<= 256 tokens).
- Embeddings used for semantic search + a supervised reranker for top-10 reordering.
- Region requirement: US-only for initial rollout (FedRAMP not required now, but SOC2 evidence requested).

Action items (owner / due)
1) SDK + auth quickstart: we will share a small sample repo and an auth flow (token rotation + service account) — owner: Jordan (3 business days).
2) Model routing / policy draft: propose primary model (smaller opt for low-cost routing) + fallback chain for degraded capacity — owner: me (Karthik) — draft attached.
3) Embeddings + reranker integration: determine embedding size and batching window; confirm whether you want on-the-fly reranking vs periodic offline refresh — owner: Integral (Samir / Priya) — reply with preference.
4) Security/compliance package: you sent a short checklist during call; please send full questionnaire (we'll map evidence) — owner: Integral.
5) Tech deep dive: 60–90m session to walk SDK auth, routing policies, and structured tool-calling (we'll show how tool calls are surfaced in the SDK) — propose Mon/Tue next week.

Attachments in this thread: integration-checklist.xlsx (template), redwood_policy_draft.yaml (routing + fallback example). I attached a draft policy below — this is intentionally high-level; we can convert into a runnable policy on the console during the deep dive.

High-level policy (excerpt)
- route_by: latency_priority
  thresholds:
    p95_latency_ms: 300
    cost_per_token_usd: 0.0009
- fallbacks:
  - model: rwd-small-quant
    when: p95 > 300 OR gpu_unavailable
  - model: rwd-medium-quant
    when: load_avg > 0.8
- region_preferences: [us-east-1, us-west-2]

Please confirm the deep dive slot and send the security questionnaire when you have it. Happy to loop in Solutions engineers as needed.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

---
Note: integration-checklist.xlsx and redwood_policy_draft.yaml are referenced; full files uploaded to shared Drive link above.

From: Samir Gupta <samir@integral.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@integral.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Integral.ai inference playbook & policy handoff

Thanks Karthik — great recap and thanks for the draft policy. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Embeddings / reranker: we prefer online reranking for freshness (1–2s window). Target vector dims: 768. We'll need guidance on batching to keep costs down.
2) Latency SLO: 300ms p95 is fine for short responses. For longer summaries (>512 tokens) acceptable p95 is 900ms.
3) Region: US-only to start; later EU expansion is possible but not in initial scope.
4) Security: attaching our full questionnaire (Integral_Security_Questionnaire.pdf). Please map the SOC2 and data-retention answers and point to where logs/artifacts will be accessible for audits.

We can do the tech deep dive on Tue 23 Nov between 11:00–12:30 ET. Also please include a brief on tool-calling: we plan to call an internal document-store vector search microservice (HTTP), and want to understand how Redwood structures tool calls and returns structured outputs.

Regards,
Samir
Head of Platform Engineering
Integral.ai

Attachment: Integral_Security_Questionnaire.pdf

Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 02:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Integral.ai inference playbook & policy handoff

Samir / Priya — thanks for the questionnaire, got it. Quick responses inline to key asks and a proposed agenda for Tue's deep dive: 

Inline responses
- Embeddings / batching: for 768-dim vectors we recommend 256-item batch window or batching by 200ms, whichever fills first. This balances throughput and per-call latency.
- Reranker approach: online rerank is supported; we recommend a hybrid where coarse embedding fetch uses a cached index and the reranker runs on top-K (k=50) live.
- Tool-calling / structured outputs: Redwood SDK supports declared tools with typed schemas. We'll demo a DocumentSearch tool (HTTP) call pattern and show how we surface structured JSON responses and errors.
- Policy draft: attached redwood_policy_draft.yaml (same as drive). It includes a sample fallback chain and cost-sensitivity flag you can toggle.

Proposed deep-dive agenda (90m)
- 0–10m: goals & success criteria (you set)
- 10–35m: SDK auth + sample repo walkthrough (Jordan leads)
- 35–65m: model routing & policy editor (me) — we'll convert the YAML into a console policy and run a simulated outage to show fallback behavior
- 65–85m: tool-calling + structured output demo (Laura leads)
- 85–90m: next steps & action items

Please confirm Tue 23 Nov 11:00 ET and I'll send a calendar invite with the repo link and pre-reads (integration-checklist.xlsx + policy draft).

Best,
Karthik

Confirmed — Tue 23 Nov 11:00 ET works for us. A couple of follow-ups so the session is efficient: 

- Please include an example of a cost-based routing rule that moves low-priority traffic to a quantized model during peak windows. We want to see how cost thresholds and latency SLOs interact in the policy UI.
- For reranker: we'll bring a small sample dataset (1000 docs) to test live. Any size limits we should be aware of for live reranking pipelines?
- On audit logs: we need per-request traces with model version, input hash, and region. Please confirm these fields are available in the Redwood audit log export.

Thanks — looking forward.

Regards,
